question: A 24-year-old woman, gravida 1, at 35 weeks gestation is admitted to the hospital with regular contractions and pelvic pressure for the last 5 hours. Her pregnancy has been uncomplicated and she has attended many prenatal appointments and followed the physician's advice about screening for diseases, laboratory testing, diet, and exercise. She has had no history of fluid leakage or bleeding. At the hospital, her temperature is 37.2°C (99.0°F), blood pressure is 108/60 mm Hg, pulse is 88/min, and respirations are 16/min. Cervical examination shows 60% effacement and 5 cm dilation with intact membranes. Cardiotocography shows a contraction amplitude of 220 MVU in 10 minutes. Which of the following is the most appropriate pharmacotherapy at this time?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Regular contractions and pelvic pressure" -> "35 weeks gestation" -> "Uncomplicated pregnancy" -> "Attended prenatal appointments and followed advice" -> "No history of fluid leakage or bleeding" -> "Temperature 37.2°C, BP 108/60 mm Hg, pulse 88/min, respirations 16/min" -> "Cervical examination: -> 60%
enhanced_information: The most appropriate pharmacotherapy at this time for the 24-year-old woman at 35 weeks gestation with regular contractions and pelvic pressure, uncomplicated pregnancy, and stable vital signs is oxytocin to augment labor progress.
analysis: Given the clinical scenario of a 24-year-old woman at 35 weeks gestation with regular contractions and cervical dilation, the most appropriate pharmacotherapy at this time, based on enhanced information and consensus, is oxytocin to augment labor progress. Oxytocin is commonly used in such situations to enhance uterine contractions and facilitate labor. Dexamethasone is typically used for fetal lung maturation in cases of preterm labor, which is not the primary concern in this scenario. Magnesium sulfate is used for neuroprotection in preterm labor or preeclampsia. Terbutaline is used for tocolysis to inhibit contractions in preterm labor. No pharmacotherapy would not be appropriate in this active labor scenario.
